transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you to the clinic today?

Hi doctor. In class and in the hospital, I keep jumping in and answering or talking before people even finish their questions, and it’s getting me into serious trouble. I'm just really stressed out because it's starting to jeopardize my spot in my radiology program.
Besides interrupting and speaking before others finish, do you also feel unusually restless or unable to stay seated, or do you mainly have trouble with impulsive talking and answering?

I definitely feel incredibly restless, especially during long lectures where my body feels like it's crawling and I have to constantly bounce my leg or get up because sitting still is unbearable. My classmates actually joke that I’m like a hummingbird because I'm constantly on the go and never seem to stop moving.
Do these symptoms happen in more than one setting, like both at school and at home or work, and have they been present since childhood?

Yes, absolutely. It happens at school and the hospital, but also at home where I can't even sit quietly through a movie with my family without constantly talking over it. This has actually been going on since elementary school, when my teachers would always send notes home about me getting out of my seat and blurting out answers.
Did these attention, impulsivity, and restlessness symptoms cause problems in school before age 12, and do they still affect your daily life now?

Yes, even before I was 12, my elementary school teachers constantly sent notes home about me getting out of my seat and struggling to wait my turn. Today, it's gotten so bad that I've received written warnings in my radiology program for my behavior. I'm actually at risk of being kicked out of the program entirely because of concerns over patient safety and professionalism.
Did these symptoms start before age 7, and have they continued without long breaks into adulthood?

Yes, they definitely started before age 7, back in kindergarten and first grade when my teachers first complained about me blurting things out and not staying in my seat. I've been constantly "on the go" without any real breaks ever since, but things became much more severe and problematic about a year and a half ago when I started my structured radiology program.
Do you also have ongoing problems with paying attention, losing things, or making careless mistakes, or is the main issue just being very restless and impulsive?

The main issue is definitely the restlessness and impulsivity, rather than losing things or being forgetful. I'm just constantly 'on the go,' blurting out answers, and physically struggling to sit still or wait my turn.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview confirms a longstanding childhood-onset pattern of hyperactivity and impulsivity across multiple settings, with clear functional impairment in school and training. Symptoms began before age 7, were present before age 12, have persisted into adulthood without remission, and include restlessness, inability to stay seated, constant motor activity, blurting out answers, and difficulty waiting turn. Inattention is not prominent, making the hyperactive/impulsive presentation most consistent with ADHD, predominantly hyperactive/impulsive type.
